  - article:
    - heading "What did we observe?" [level=2]
    - paragraph: The arcs from P cut line l at A and B.
    - paragraph: Joining A and B forms a line that meets l at a right angle (90°).
    - img: P A B l
  - article:
    - heading "Notice the pattern" [level=2]
    - paragraph: ✓ Arc centered at P gives two equidistant points A and B.
    - paragraph: ✓ Line AB passes through P.
    - paragraph: ✓ AB is perpendicular to l.
    - paragraph: ✓ Works for both on-line and off-line cases.
  - article:
    - heading "Key Rule" [level=2]
    - complementary:
      - text: Perpendicular Through a Point Rule
      - paragraph: With center at the given point P, draw an arc that cuts the given line l at two points A and B. Join A and B.
      - strong: Then AB ⟂ l and ∠(AB, l) = 90°.
  - complementary:
    - heading "⚠ Common Mistake" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Not using the same center (P) for the arc. The arc must be centered at P so that the distances PA and PB are equal.
    - heading "☀ Why it matters" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Equal distances from P to A and P to B guarantee that AB is perpendicular to l.
  - article:
    - heading "Worked Example" [level=2]
    - paragraph: "Construction: Draw a line perpendicular to line l through point P below line l."
    - list:
      - listitem: Draw an arc centered at P cutting line l at A and B.
      - listitem: Join A and B to get line AB.
      - listitem: Then AB ⟂ l.
    - img: P A
    - complementary:
      - text: Verified
      - paragraph: ✓ ∠(AB, l) = 90°
      - paragraph: ✓ Construction is correct.
  - article:
    - heading "Formula / Definition" [level=2]
    - heading "Definition" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Two lines are perpendicular if they intersect to form a right angle.
    - heading "Symbolically" [level=3]
    - strong: AB ⟂ l ⇔ ∠(AB, l) = 90°
    - heading "Steps (Summary)" [level=3]
    - list:
      - listitem: With center P, draw an arc cutting l at A and B.
      - listitem: Join A and B.
      - listitem: AB is perpendicular to l.
